# Preserver — Full Site Content

> Complete text content of every major page. Updated: 2026-08-25.

**App:** Preserver — professional GPS timestamped capture app for iOS and Android
**Website:** https://preserver.me
**App Store:** https://apps.apple.com/au/app/preserver/id6443649784
**Google Play:** https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=au.com.preserverapp.preserver&hl=en
**AU Address:** Brisbane, Australia
**US Address:** Preserver LLC, Sunnyvale, California, USA
**Rating:** 4.9 stars on Google Play
**Price:** Capture is free — no registration, unlimited captures. AI-ready export bundles free during beta; beta users grandfathered (keep free access permanently); small monthly Pro charge for new users in future.
**Privacy:** No account required. No data sold. Captures stored on-device only.
**AI:** Preserver exports structured, AI-ready data bundles (JSON manifest, transcripts, media, GPS, timestamps, SHA-256 hashes) for use with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, NotebookLM or custom pipelines. Preserver never sends data to any AI automatically and never trains AI on user captures — the user chooses which AI receives an exported bundle.

**URL:** https://preserver.me/

AI-ready. ★ 4.9 Google Play | 100+ active users | Free capture, always Not sure what "Preserver" means? What is Preserver? If you're searching for the meaning of "preserver" as a life-saving flotation device, or as something used in food preservation, this isn't that. Preserver is a mobile app for iOS and Android that turns your phone into a real-world data collector. It captures photos, video, voice recordings and text notes, and automatically stamps every one with the exact time, date and GPS location — creating a verifiable record of when and where something happened. Then it does what no camera roll can: it exports everything as a structured, AI-ready bundle — media, transcripts, locations, timestamps and integrity hashes in machine-readable format. Drop the bundle into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok or NotebookLM and turn a day in the field into a finished report in minutes. Capture is free, works offline, and needs no registration. Download Preserver → Why Preserver? Everything you need to preserve your activities 📡 Works Offline No Wi-Fi. No Bluetooth. No mobile data. Capture with full metadata anywhere — underground, in the air, or miles from the nearest tower. 📍 Verified Ground Truth Every capture carries irrefutable time, date and GPS metadata, protected by SHA-256 integrity hashes. AI outputs are only as good as their inputs — Preserver makes your inputs provable. 🤖 AI-Ready Exports One tap exports your whole activity as a structured bundle: JSON manifest, voice transcripts, media, locations and timestamps. Built to be read by ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok — or your own tools. 🔒 Private by Design No registration. No account. Your data stays on your device — and we never use your captures to train AI. ## FAQ
**URL:** https://preserver.me/faq/

FAQ Frequently Asked Questions Everything you need to know about Preserver — pricing, privacy, AI-ready exports, features and platforms. Pricing & Purchase How much does Preserver cost? Capturing with Preserver is completely free — on both the App Store and Google Play. Unlimited photo, video, voice and text captures, full GPS and timestamp metadata, offline operation, local or personal-cloud storage. AI-ready export bundles are also free while they're in beta. In future, new users will pay a small monthly charge for the Pro version — but you never pay to capture or to access your own data. Is capture really free forever? Yes. Every capture feature is free and stays free — no capture limits, no metadata locked behind a paywall, no renewal fees. AI-ready export bundles are currently free too, while in beta. When the Pro version launches with a small monthly charge, it will apply to new users only. What does Preserver Pro include? Preserver Pro covers AI-analysis export bundles: a machine-readable JSON manifest, voice-note transcripts, all media files, GPS coordinates, timestamps and SHA-256 integrity hashes packaged together — ready to drop into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, NotebookLM or your own data pipeline. Pro is free during the beta. In future it will carry a small monthly charge for new users, and export bundles remain included in enterprise white-label packages. Will I be charged when the beta ends? No. If you use Preserver's AI-ready exports during the beta, you're grandfathered in — your access stays free when the paid Pro version launches. The future small monthly charge applies to new Pro users only. Early users are rewarded, not penalised. Do I need to create an account or register? No account or registration is required to use Preserver. Just download it from the App Store or Google Play. We never ask for your name, email or any personal details. Future Pro billing will be handled through your App Store or Google Play account, not a Preserver account. Privacy & Data Where is my data stored? On your device, by default. If you choose, you can store your Activities in your personal cloud account (Google Drive, iCloud, Dropbox, etc.). You're always in control — nothing is shared with anyone unless you actively choose to share it. Do you share my data with third parties? Never. Preserver does not sell your data or use it to train AI models — ours or anyone else's. Your captures stay on your device or in your own cloud. If you export an AI-ready bundle, you choose which AI service receives it, under your own account and their terms. No ad platform has access to your captures or personal data. Can I use AI tools on my captured data? Yes — that's exactly what Preserver's AI-ready export bundles are designed for (free during beta). Export an activity as a structured bundle and upload it to ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, NotebookLM or any AI tool that accepts file uploads. Preserver itself never sends anything to any AI automatically — you decide what leaves your device, when, and where it goes. See the AI-Ready Exports section below for details. Can Preserver see my captures? No. Your captures are stored on your device and, if you choose, in your own cloud account. Preserver as a company has no access to what you record. There is no server where your content is uploaded to us. What happens to my data if I delete the app? Your data is stored on your device, so deleting the app removes it from that device. If you've backed up to a personal cloud account (Google Drive, iCloud, etc.), your captures remain there under your control. AI-Ready Exports What is an AI-ready export bundle? A single package containing everything from an activity: a machine-readable JSON manifest, voice-note transcripts, all photos and video, GPS coordinates, timestamps, and SHA-256 hashes that prove nothing was altered after capture. It's designed to be understood by any modern AI assistant or data pipeline — real-world ground truth, structured for machines. Which AI tools work with Preserver exports? Any tool that accepts file uploads — ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, Microsoft Copilot, NotebookLM — plus custom pipelines via the JSON manifest. You're never locked to one AI vendor: the bundle format is open and readable by anything. Why does AI need "ground truth" data? AI models generate fluent text but can't verify what happened in the real world. Preserver gives your AI verified inputs — what was seen, said, when and where, with integrity hashes — so the output is grounded in fact instead of guesswork. If it's in the report, it was captured in the field. Does Preserver run AI on my device or send my data to AI automatically? No. Preserver captures and packages — nothing more. Nothing is sent to any AI unless you personally export a bundle and upload it yourself. Speech-to-text uses your phone's native on-device recognition, not a cloud service. What can I create from an export bundle? Whatever your AI can write from verified inputs: site inspection reports, incident summaries, compliance records, case timelines, meeting minutes, client updates, even blog posts and social content — all grounded in timestamped, geolocated observations rather than memory or guesswork. Features & Capture What types of media can I capture? Text notes, voice recordings, photos, and video — all within a single Activity entry. Everything is automatically stamped with date, time and GPS at the moment of capture. What metadata is captured automatically? Every capture is automatically stamped with date, time, and GPS coordinates. Unlike most apps, this metadata stays embedded in your data even when you export or share it — so your proof of time and location travels with the record. Does it work without an internet connection? Absolutely. Preserver works completely offline — no Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, or mobile data required. GPS capture works via satellite with no network connection at all. Your captures are stored on your device until you choose to back them up or share them. Does GPS work without mobile signal? Yes. GPS positioning uses satellites, not mobile towers or Wi-Fi. It works underground, in aircraft, in remote areas, and anywhere else there is no mobile or data signal. This is one of Preserver's most important features for field users. What is an Activity? An Activity is a container for a related set of captures — for example, a job site visit, a field research session, or a day's notes. Within each Activity you can mix text, voice, photos and video, all sharing the same timestamp and location context. How do I export or share my captures? From within any Activity, you can share directly to other apps, export to your cloud storage, or send via email or messaging. You control exactly what gets shared and with whom. The GPS and timestamp metadata travels with the export. Can I add notes after the fact? Yes, you can add additional captures to an Activity at any time. The original captures retain their original timestamps, so the record of when each item was captured is always accurate and tamper-evident. AI & Transcription Does Preserver send my audio to any AI service? No. Preserver never uploads your recordings anywhere. These features use the AI already built into your phone by Apple or Google. You choose when and whether to share a file with it. Does this work offline? Recording and exporting in Preserver always work offline. Apple Intelligence transcription and Notes summaries run on-device. Gemini generally requires an internet connection; Pixel Recorder transcription runs on-device. Is my exported recording still valid as evidence after transcription? Your original recording in Preserver is untouched — transcription and summarisation work on the exported copy. Keep the original in Preserver (or your export bundle, which includes the timestamped metadata) as your source of record. What languages are supported? Transcription language support depends on your phone's speech recognition, not on Preserver. Check your device's language settings — on iPhone under Settings → General → Language & Region, and on Android under your speech/voice input settings. Which phones support this? Apple Intelligence requires iPhone 15 Pro or later running a current version of iOS. Gemini is available on most recent Android phones; on-device summarisation features vary by model. Older phones can still transcribe using Notes (iPhone) or share the file to any transcription app of your choice. Do I need to pay for anything? No. Apple Intelligence and Gemini's core features are included with your phone, capturing with Preserver is completely free, and AI-ready exports are free during the beta. This workflow adds nothing to that. My exported video won't open in Gemini — why? Make sure you're sharing the file directly from Preserver's share sheet, and that you're running the latest version of Preserver. If a file won't open in another app, contact us and we'll help. Platforms & Compatibility Is Preserver available on iOS and Android? Yes — Preserver is available on both the Apple App Store and Google Play Store, free to capture on each. Is there a desktop or web version? Currently Preserver is a mobile app for iOS and Android. Your captures can be accessed on desktop by exporting them to your cloud storage (Google Drive, iCloud, Dropbox) and opening them on any device. What iOS and Android versions are supported? Preserver supports iOS 15 and above, and Android 8 and above. For the best experience, we recommend keeping your device's OS updated to the latest version. Can I use Preserver on multiple devices? Yes. Because there's no account, each device operates independently. If you back up to a shared cloud account (e.g., family Google Drive), captures from multiple devices can be stored together. Direct cross-device sync is on our roadmap. Professional & Compliance Use Can I use Preserver for professional or compliance purposes? Yes. Preserver is used across 40+ industries for timestamped evidence, field records, compliance documentation, and more. The automatic GPS and timestamp metadata makes it suitable for evidence-grade capture in many professional contexts. Is the timestamp tamper-proof? The timestamp is captured at the device level at the moment of recording and is not editable within the app. While no digital timestamp is fully tamper-proof in an absolute legal sense, the metadata is embedded and travels with the file, making alterations detectable. For critical legal matters, consult a legal professional. Can Preserver be used as legal evidence? Preserver captures are increasingly used to support legal matters — disputes, insurance claims, workplace incidents and more. Whether records are accepted as evidence depends on the jurisdiction and the context. The GPS and timestamp metadata significantly strengthens the credibility of any capture. Consult a legal professional for your specific situation. Still have questions? Free to capture. No registration, no signal needed. AI exports free during beta — early users keep them free forever. Or send us a message — we read every one.

## Blog: Why GPS Metadata Matters
**URL:** https://preserver.me/blog/gps-metadata/

← All articles How-to June 2026 5 min read Why GPS Metadata Matters More Than You Think Your phone embeds GPS coordinates into every photo — but most apps silently strip them when you share. Here's why keeping that metadata is a bigger deal than most people realise. Every photo taken on a modern smartphone contains more than just pixels. Buried in each image file is a block of EXIF metadata — the date, time, camera settings, and critically, the precise GPS coordinates of where the photo was taken. Most people know this exists. Fewer realise how quickly it disappears. Where the metadata goes When you upload a photo to social media, the platform strips the GPS data before showing it publicly — a sensible privacy measure. When you send a photo through most messaging apps, the same thing happens. By the time an image reaches the person you sent it to, the location information is often already gone. This is fine for sharing holiday photos with family. It becomes a real problem when the photo is evidence. Why location proof matters Consider a few everyday situations where GPS metadata isn't just useful — it's essential: A tradesperson photographs completed work at a client's property. If there's a later dispute about whether the job was done, or done on time, an image stripped of its location is far less useful than one that proves exactly where and when it was taken. A compliance officer documents a site inspection. Their report is only as strong as the evidence behind it. Photos with embedded coordinates and timestamps that can't be edited after the fact carry real weight. A carer records an incident at a facility. The time and location of that record can matter legally — and that information needs to survive being shared with a supervisor or insurer. What Preserver does differently Preserver captures text notes, voice recordings, photos and video — and embeds the timestamp and GPS coordinates at the moment of capture , not as editable fields you fill in later. The metadata travels with the record when you export or share it. This isn't magic — it's just not stripping something your phone already provides. But that small difference is meaningful when the record needs to hold up. The best evidence is the kind that doesn't require you to explain where it came from. The timestamp and location speak for themselves. Works offline too GPS location doesn't require mobile data or Wi-Fi — it works via satellite. Preserver captures location even when you're completely off the grid, which matters for anyone working in remote areas, underground, or in buildings with poor signal. The short version Your phone is already collecting this data. Most apps throw it away. Preserver keeps it, attaches it permanently to your capture, and makes sure it's still there when you need it. That's the whole point. Get Preserver — Free Free to download. No subscription. No signal needed.

## Blog: How Tradespeople Use Timestamped Photos
**URL:** https://preserver.me/blog/tradies/

← All articles Use cases May 2026 4 min read How Tradespeople Use Timestamped Photos to Protect Themselves A single timestamped before/after photo can resolve a customer dispute in minutes. We look at how tradies across Australia use Preserver to document jobs and stay protected. Trades disputes are one of the most common small business headaches in Australia. A customer claims the work wasn't done properly, or wasn't done at all. A scope creep argument erupts. Someone insists the damage was pre-existing. Without documentation, it's your word against theirs — and that's a stressful place to be. An increasing number of tradies have found a simple answer: photograph everything, and make sure the photo proves where and when it was taken. The before/after photo is your best witness A photo taken before you start work — showing the existing condition of a wall, pipe, roof, or wiring — combined with one taken after completion, with embedded GPS coordinates and an uneditable timestamp, is a powerful record. It proves you were at that address, at that time, and that the job was completed in the condition you're claiming. Most tradies already take job photos. The issue is that photos sent via text or email often lose their metadata, and photos stored in a general camera roll aren't always easy to retrieve months later when a dispute arises. I used to just take photos on my phone and hope I could find them later. Now every job gets its own activity in Preserver — before, during, after. Takes two extra minutes and has saved me from a few very awkward conversations. What tradies capture in Preserver Arrival photo — shows the property, the date, and sometimes the clock on a wall if you want belt-and-braces proof Pre-work condition — existing damage, wear, or issues before you touch anything During-work progress shots — useful for complex or multi-day jobs Completion photos — the finished work in its final state Voice note summary — a quick spoken debrief of what was done, any issues encountered, and what the customer said at handover No Wi-Fi required on site A lot of trade work happens in areas with poor mobile signal — underground, in new developments, in remote properties. Preserver captures all metadata via GPS satellite, which doesn't need a network connection. Everything syncs when you're back in coverage. It's not just about disputes Good documentation also helps with insurance claims, warranty work, quoting future jobs based on documented past work, and simply running a more professional operation. Clients notice when a tradie arrives prepared and leaves with a clear record of what was done. It builds trust. The barrier to doing this properly used to be that it required extra effort — a separate app, a folder system, manual uploads. Preserver makes it as fast as pulling out your phone. Which is what you're already doing. Start documenting your jobs Free to download. No subscription. No registration.

## Blog: Field Research Without Wi-Fi
**URL:** https://preserver.me/blog/offline-field/

← All articles Use cases April 2026 5 min read Field Research Without Wi-Fi: Preserver in Remote Australia Researchers, farmers and field workers operating in areas without mobile coverage share how offline-first capture has changed their documentation workflow. Australia is a continent with long stretches of country where mobile coverage ranges from patchy to nonexistent. For the researchers, ecologists, agricultural workers, and inspectors who work in these areas, apps that depend on a network connection are frustrating at best and useless at worst. Preserver was built to work offline — not as a workaround, but as a core design principle. GPS positioning works via satellite, independent of any network. Captures are stored locally on the device. Nothing requires a connection at the time of capture. Environmental monitoring in the field Environmental consultants conducting baseline surveys often work in national parks, coastal reserves, or agricultural land far from towers. Their workflow requires capturing precise location data for every observation — a photo of a species, a voice note about ground cover, a text entry about water quality at a specific coordinate. The alternative — handwritten notes to be transcribed later, GPS devices carried separately, cameras that record nothing beyond the image — is slow, error-prone and produces records that are harder to defend in a regulatory context. We're often three hours from the nearest town. The last thing I want to be doing is worrying about whether my phone has signal. Preserver just works. Everything is there when I get back. Agricultural property inspection Property managers and agronomists covering large rural properties face similar challenges. Documenting fence lines, water infrastructure, crop conditions, or weed infestations across thousands of hectares means a full day of captures that need to be associated with specific map coordinates. Preserver's GPS capture means every photo and note is automatically pinned to the location where it was taken, even when there's no signal. When the device reconnects — back at the homestead, on the road home — everything is available to review, export, or share. The sync-later model A common pattern among field workers is what we call "capture now, sort later." The field session is purely about getting good records — photos, voice notes, observations — with GPS stamps on everything. Back at the office or home, those records are reviewed, organised, and either kept locally or backed up to a personal cloud account. This workflow doesn't require Preserver to be connected to anything at any point except during the optional cloud backup step. And that backup goes to your own cloud account — Google Drive, iCloud, Dropbox — not to any Preserver server. What offline-first actually means No network required to capture text, audio, photos, or video GPS coordinates recorded via satellite, not cell-tower triangulation All captures stored securely on your device No data leaves your device unless you actively export or sync Works the same on day one of a week-long remote survey as it does in the city For anyone who spends time working beyond the edge of coverage, this isn't a feature — it's the whole point. Works anywhere. Even out there. Free to download. Offline-capable. No registration.

## Blog: Voice Notes vs Typed Notes
**URL:** https://preserver.me/blog/voice-vs-text/

← All articles Features April 2026 3 min read Voice Notes vs Typed Notes: When to Use Each Both are GPS-tagged and timestamped in Preserver, but voice and text serve different capture situations. Here's a practical guide to choosing the right one on the job. Preserver supports four capture types: text, voice, photo, and video. All four get the same automatic timestamp and GPS tag. But when it comes to day-to-day capture, most people find themselves reaching for either their keyboard or the microphone — and the choice usually comes down to situation, not preference. When voice notes win Voice recording is faster when your hands are occupied. A tradie on a ladder can dictate what they're seeing without stopping work. A carer entering a facility can speak a quick observation note while walking. A researcher in the field can narrate what they're photographing without putting the camera down. Voice is also better for nuance. Tone, emphasis, and context come through in a voice note in a way that a typed sentence can't always convey. If you're recounting a conversation, describing a complex scene, or summarising a meeting, speaking naturally produces a richer record than typing quickly. Hands are occupied or gloved You need to capture quickly — voice is faster than typing for most people The content is conversational or narrative You're in low light where typing is awkward You want to capture tone or inflection When typed notes win Text is better when the record will be searched, scanned, or shared. A typed note is immediately readable at a glance — in a list view, in an export, in a report. Voice notes require playback. Text is also more precise for numbers, names, codes, or technical terms. Dictating "the serial number is BE-7-7-4-2-slash-Q" takes longer and is error-prone. Typing it takes three seconds. The content includes codes, numbers, or proper nouns You're in a quiet environment where speaking aloud would be awkward The note will be reviewed quickly without playback You need to record something brief and factual Combining both Nothing stops you from using both types in the same activity. A photo of a damaged component, followed by a typed note with the part number, followed by a voice summary of what happened — that's a complete record that covers different kinds of information efficiently. The best capture is the one you actually make. Use whichever method means you don't skip the record entirely. Both give you the same GPS and timestamp. Both are stored privately on your device. The choice is purely about what works best in the moment. Get Preserver — Free Text, voice, photo, video — all GPS-tagged and timestamped. Free to download.
